options.text: Deploys an AVD landing zone: virtual networks, an FSLogix storage account, Log Analytics, host pools and their session hosts. What gets built depends on the choices on the next two tabs - cloud-only or hybrid identities, VNets created here or ones you already have, and whether there is a hub.

FSLogix uses Microsoft Entra Kerberos either way, so session hosts must be Entra joined and running Windows 11 24H2 or later, or Windows Server 2025 - and at or above Microsoft's minimum cumulative update, which a fresh marketplace image does not necessarily meet. Under the hybrid identity model this template builds the landing zone without session hosts: you add a domain controller afterwards and create the hosts separately.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: Region for all resources. AVD metadata is supported in US and European regions, among others.

options.text:
Optional - leave it empty and nothing is tagged.

One row is one tag: Name is the key, Value is its value, both used exactly as typed. Every tag listed here is applied to everything this deployment creates - all of the resource groups, and every resource inside them that supports tags. They are not divided up between resources, and there is no way to tag one resource group differently from another.

Empty rows are ignored. The grey text in one is an example of the shape, not a value.
Subnets, peerings, role assignments, diagnostic settings and data collection rule associations cannot carry tags. That is an Azure limitation, so coverage is never quite complete.

elements.name: identityModel
elements.label: Identity model
elements.toolTip: Where the user accounts and groups live. Everything else on this tab, and the DNS servers on the Spokes tab, follow from this choice.

allowedValues.label: Hybrid (on-premises AD synced to Entra ID)

options.text: Hybrid builds the landing zone WITHOUT session hosts: networks, storage, monitoring, the host pools, application groups and workspace are all created, and the hosts are not. Add a domain controller afterwards, then create the session hosts with your usual process. Host pool rows on the AVD tab are still honoured - the pools are created and left empty.

elements.name: hybridDomainControllerReady
elements.label: The domain controller exists and Entra Connect is syncing
elements.toolTip: Leave unticked on the first deployment. The Entra Kerberos setup is deferred until the domain controller is in place and users are synced, because it cannot work before then.

options.text: Entra Kerberos will be deferred. The storage account is created without AADKERB and no admin consent is granted, because both need users already synced from Active Directory. Build the domain controller into the hub identity subnet, get Entra Connect running, then redeploy with the box above ticked. Profiles will not mount until then, which is expected on a first pass.

elements.name: dnsServers
elements.label: DNS servers for every VNet
elements.toolTip: The domain controllers. Every VNet this template creates will use them. They must forward to 168.63.129.16, or the storage account resolves to its public IP and profiles stop mounting.

constraints.validationMessage: One or more IP addresses, separated by commas.

options.text: Creating Entra groups and finishing the Entra Kerberos setup are Microsoft Graph operations, and the portal's deployment flow carries no Graph token. Supplying a managed identity that holds the right Graph permissions lets the deployment do that work itself. Without one, everything here has to be done by hand afterwards.

Create the identity once per tenant with scripts/bootstrap-entra-identity.ps1 from the repository - granting its Graph permissions needs Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator. To fetch the resource ID again later, run scripts/get-identity-id.ps1, which prints it and copies it to the clipboard.

elements.name: useEntraManagedIdentity
elements.label: Use the bootstrap managed identity
elements.toolTip: Four steps here are Microsoft Graph operations a portal deployment cannot do by itself: creating the access groups, granting admin consent on the storage account's Entra application, tagging it for cloud group SIDs, and renaming the published desktop. A deployment script running as this managed identity can. It is found by name, so there is nothing to enter. Leave it ticked unless scripts/bootstrap-entra-identity.ps1 has never been run in this tenant - ticked with no identity present fails the deployment partway through; unticked skips all four steps and you do them by hand.

options.text: With no identity, the deployment cannot create groups, grant admin consent on the storage account's Entra application, or tag it for cloud-only group SIDs. Profiles will not mount until all three are done manually. Supply existing group object IDs below so at least the role assignments are made.

elements.name: createEntraGroups
elements.label: Create the AVD access groups
elements.toolTip: Groups are matched by display name, so redeploying reuses them rather than creating duplicates.

elements.name: avdUsersGroupName
elements.label: Users group name
elements.toolTip: Gets Desktop Virtualization User on each application group, Virtual Machine User Login on the session hosts, and SMB Share Contributor on the profile share.

elements.name: avdAdminsGroupName
elements.label: Admins group name
elements.toolTip: Gets Virtual Machine Administrator Login and SMB Share Elevated Contributor.

options.text: Groups created here are cloud-only: they hold synced users and carry Azure RBAC fine, but they cannot be managed from on-premises AD, and their SIDs are cloud SIDs. Once session hosts exist, file-level NTFS permissions on the profile share resolve group SIDs from the user's Kerberos ticket, which for a hybrid identity carries the SIDs of its AD groups - so for NTFS specifically a synced AD group is the safer choice. Share-level access is unaffected.
Object IDs, not names. Leave blank to skip the role assignments - but without the users group the desktop will not appear in anyone's client, and nobody can sign in to a session host.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a GUID, or leave blank.
Enter a GUID, or leave blank.

elements.name: configureEntraKerberos
elements.label: Finish the Entra Kerberos setup on the storage account
elements.toolTip: Grants admin consent on the application Azure creates for the storage account, and adds the kdc_enable_cloud_group_sids tag. Both are mandatory for cloud-only identities - without the tag, authentication to the share fails.

elements.name: setFslogixNtfsPermissions
elements.label: Set NTFS permissions on the profile share
elements.toolTip: Runs on the first session host. Azure RBAC decides who reaches the share; NTFS decides what they can do on it, and the defaults let every user open every other user's profile.

options.text: One step always remains manual: exclude the storage account's Entra application from any Conditional Access policy requiring MFA. Entra Kerberos does not support MFA, and a broad policy produces 'System error 1327' when users load their profile. The application ID appears in the deployment outputs.

elements.name: networkMode
elements.label: Virtual networks
elements.toolTip: Create the VNets from the Spokes and Subnets tabs, or point at ones that already exist.

elements.name: existingSessionHostSubnetId
elements.label: Session host subnet ID
elements.toolTip: Full resource ID of the subnet the session hosts go in.

constraints.validationMessage: Must be a full subnet resource ID.

elements.name: existingPrivateEndpointSubnetId
elements.label: Private endpoint subnet ID
elements.placeholder: Leave empty to skip the private endpoint
elements.toolTip: Where the FSLogix private endpoint lands. May be the same subnet. Empty means the share is reached over its public endpoint.

constraints.validationMessage: Must be a full subnet resource ID, or empty.

elements.name: avdResourceGroupName
elements.label: AVD resource group
elements.toolTip: Created for the host pool, application group, workspace and session hosts.

elements.name: hubMode
elements.label: Hub
elements.toolTip: A hub carries the gateway, the firewall and any domain controllers. Microsoft's model is to peer into one the customer already has; creating one is for a greenfield site where nobody else will.

options.text: Microsoft's model is to peer into a hub the customer already has: a hub carries their gateway, firewall and domain controllers, and belongs to whoever runs their network. Creating one here means owning a piece of that design. Correct for a greenfield site where nobody else will build it; think twice where they already have Azure.

elements.name: hubRgName
elements.label: Resource group name
elements.toolTip: Named exactly as you type it.

elements.name: hubVnetName
elements.label: VNet name
elements.toolTip: Named exactly as you type it.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a CIDR range, such as 10.0.0.0/16.

elements.name: gatewaySubnetPrefix
elements.label: GatewaySubnet prefix
elements.toolTip: Created whether or not a gateway is deployed - adding it later means resizing the VNet.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a CIDR range.

elements.name: identitySubnetName
elements.label: Identity subnet name
elements.toolTip: For domain controllers. Named exactly as you type it.

elements.name: identitySubnetPrefix
elements.label: Identity subnet prefix
elements.toolTip: A hybrid deployment needs this: the domain controller is built into it after the landing zone.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a CIDR range, or leave empty.

elements.name: hubFirewallType
elements.label: Hub firewall
elements.toolTip: Selecting one makes it the egress path for every created VNet, overriding the outbound choice below.

allowedValues.label: Azure Firewall - deployed with AVD egress rules
FortiGate - subnets only, appliance deployed separately

elements.name: azureFirewallTier
elements.label: Tier
elements.toolTip: Basic tops out at 250 Mbps and needs a management subnet with a second public IP, unconditionally.

elements.name: azureFirewallSubnetPrefix
elements.label: AzureFirewallSubnet prefix
elements.toolTip: /26 minimum. The name is fixed by Azure.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a CIDR range of /26 or larger.

elements.name: azureFirewallManagementSubnetPrefix
elements.label: AzureFirewallManagementSubnet prefix
elements.toolTip: Basic needs a management NIC in its own subnet with a second public IP.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a CIDR range, or leave empty.

elements.name: hubFirewallInternalIp
elements.label: Appliance internal IP
elements.toolTip: The template does not deploy the appliance and cannot discover this. Route tables point here.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter an IPv4 address.
Enter a CIDR range.

elements.name: fgtInternalPrefix
elements.label: Internal subnet
elements.toolTip: The appliance's internal IP must sit inside this range.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a CIDR range.
Enter a CIDR range.
Enter a CIDR range.

elements.name: fgtExternalSubnetName
elements.label: External subnet name
elements.toolTip: Named exactly as you type it.

elements.name: fgtInternalSubnetName
elements.label: Internal subnet name
elements.toolTip: Named exactly as you type it.

elements.name: fgtHaSubnetName
elements.label: HA subnet name
elements.toolTip: Named exactly as you type it.

elements.name: fgtMgmtSubnetName
elements.label: Management subnet name
elements.toolTip: Named exactly as you type it.

elements.name: deployBastionSubnet
elements.label: Create AzureBastionSubnet
elements.toolTip: The subnet only. No Bastion host is deployed by this template.

elements.name: bastionSubnetPrefix
elements.label: AzureBastionSubnet prefix
elements.toolTip: /26 minimum - Azure rejects anything smaller.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a CIDR range of /26 or larger, or leave empty.

elements.name: peerToExistingHubVnetId
elements.label: Hub VNet resource ID
elements.toolTip: Each VNet with Peer to hub set on the Spokes tab is peered to this one. The hub side of the peering can only be created when the hub is in this subscription.

constraints.validationMessage: Must be a full VNet resource ID, or empty.

elements.name: egressMode
elements.label: Outbound internet
elements.toolTip: Session hosts reach the AVD service over the internet to register, so a host with no egress never comes up.

options.text: Set Create NAT gateway to Yes on each VNet that needs it, and Use NAT gateway to Yes on its subnets. A gateway with no subnet attached does nothing. Microsoft recommends this over a firewall for AVD: routing the service traffic through an inspection device costs performance.

elements.name: firewallPrivateIp
elements.label: Firewall private IP
elements.toolTip: A route table per VNet sends 0.0.0.0/0 here. The firewall itself is not created.

constraints.validationMessage: Must be an IPv4 address.

options.text: The spoke key links subnets to their parent VNet on the Subnets tab - it is not a resource name. Name the resource group and the VNet exactly as you want them in the next two columns.
Leave Resource group name or VNet name blank and they fall back to rg-<key> and vnet-<key>. Exactly one spoke should have the AVD role: the session hosts and the FSLogix private endpoint land there.

Every VNet that needs outbound internet must have its own NAT gateway - set Create NAT gateway to Yes here, and Use NAT gateway to Yes on its subnets. Session hosts reach the AVD service over the internet to register, so a host pool in a VNet without egress is skipped rather than built into a state where it can never come up.

validations.message: Short identifier: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 2 to 16 characters. Example: avd. Not a full resource name.
Enter a CIDR range, for example 10.3.0.0/16.

element.name: peerToHub
element.toolTip: Only has an effect when a hub is created or an existing one is given on the Network tab.

options.text: A NAT gateway cannot be shared between virtual networks, so each spoke with one pays for its own gateway and public IP. Not needed when a hub firewall provides outbound access - and do not use both on the same subnet, because the route table wins and the NAT gateway bills for nothing.
Not used: you chose existing VNets on the Network tab, so nothing on this tab or the Subnets tab is created. The subnets you named there are used as they are.
One row per subnet. Parent VNet is the Spoke key from the Spokes tab - it says which VNet the subnet is created in. Everything else describes the subnet itself.

Parent spoke key must match a Spoke key from the Spokes tab exactly. New rows are pre-filled with the first one, but it is not corrected for you, and a row pointing at a spoke that does not exist fails the deployment partway through. The AVD spoke needs one subnet with NSG rules set to 'AVD' - the session hosts go there - and one with Private endpoint set to Yes, which is where the FSLogix endpoint lands. The same subnet can do both.

validations.message: Must exactly match a Spoke identifier from the Spokes tab, for example avd.

element.toolTip: The Spoke key from the Spokes tab, character for character. Not the VNet's name.

validations.message: Short identifier: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 2 to 24 characters. Example: hosts.

element.toolTip: Named exactly as you type it. Its network security group is called nsg-<this name>.

validations.message: Enter a CIDR range, for example 10.3.0.0/24.

options.text: The AVD baseline NSG documents the outbound destinations AVD needs. It does not restrict egress - Azure's default rules still allow outbound internet. Real egress control needs a firewall or explicit deny rules.
Not used with existing VNets. The session host and private endpoint subnets come from the Network tab.

elements.name: deployStorage
elements.label: Deploy FSLogix storage
elements.toolTip: Storage account, SMB share, private endpoint and private DNS zone.

elements.name: storageRgName
elements.label: Storage resource group name
elements.toolTip: Must not match any spoke name.

elements.name: storageAccountName
elements.label: Storage account name
elements.toolTip: Must be globally unique across all of Azure.

constraints.validationMessage: Lowercase letters and digits only, 3 to 24 characters, globally unique.

elements.name: storageSku
elements.label: Redundancy
elements.toolTip: Premium is strongly recommended for FSLogix profile performance.

constraints.validationMessage: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 3 to 63 characters.

elements.name: fileShareQuotaGiB
elements.label: Share quota (GiB)
elements.toolTip: Premium shares are provisioned - you pay for the quota, not what is used.

options.text: Entra Kerberos is enabled on the account automatically. Granting admin consent, tagging the app for cloud-only group SIDs and setting NTFS permissions on the share all happen too, provided a managed identity is supplied on the Entra ID tab. Excluding the storage app from MFA Conditional Access stays manual.

elements.name: deployMonitoring
elements.label: Deploy Log Analytics
elements.toolTip: Workspace plus diagnostic settings on every virtual network, the storage account and the AVD control plane.

elements.name: monitoringRgName
elements.label: Monitoring resource group name
elements.toolTip: Must not match any spoke name.

options.text: Infrastructure diagnostics only. AVD Insights additionally needs monitoring agents and data collection rules on the session hosts, which this template does not deploy.

elements.name: deployAvdInsights
elements.label: Collect session host telemetry for AVD Insights
elements.toolTip: Azure Monitor Agent on each host plus a data collection rule with Microsoft's AVD counter and event set, including the FSLogix channels.

elements.name: collectPerProcessInputDelay
elements.label: Also collect per-process input delay
elements.toolTip: Instances scale with processes times sessions. A large share of ingestion cost for detail you rarely act on.

elements.name: deployAlerts
elements.label: Deploy the starter alert set
elements.toolTip: Session host availability, connection failure rate, FSLogix errors, disk space, CPU and memory.

elements.name: alertEmailAddress
elements.label: Alert email address
elements.toolTip: Leave blank and the alerts still fire and appear in the portal, but nobody is notified.

constraints.validationMessage: An email address, or blank.

elements.name: alertActionGroupShortName
elements.label: Action group short name
elements.toolTip: Appears in alert emails and texts. Azure caps it at 12 characters.

constraints.validationMessage: Letters and digits, up to 12 characters.

options.text: Each host pool is pooled with depth-first load balancing and gets its own desktop application group. All application groups appear inside the single workspace. Leave the grid empty to skip the control plane entirely.

validations.message: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 2 to 24 characters.

options.text: Check core quota for the size family in this region before deploying. Quota is per family, defaults to zero for many of them, and a shortfall fails validation rather than the deployment. Run: az vm list-usage --location <region> --output table. All sizes listed support Trusted Launch, which the session hosts require; v3 and older families do not.

elements.name: avdWorkspaceFriendlyName
elements.label: Workspace display name
elements.toolTip: What users see when they subscribe in the AVD client.

options.text: Session hosts are not created under the hybrid identity model, because there is no domain controller for them to join yet. The host pools defined above, their application groups and the workspace are all created and left empty. Add a domain controller, then create the hosts with your usual process and register them against these pools.

elements.name: deploySessionHosts
elements.label: Deploy session hosts
elements.toolTip: Unticked builds the host pools, application groups and workspace with no VMs, ignoring the session host count on each row above.

options.text: Hosts are built from Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session 25H2 with Microsoft 365 Apps, joined to Entra ID, and registered with their host pool automatically. They land in the AVD spoke's subnet that uses the AVD NSG rule set.

elements.name: adminUsername
elements.label: Local administrator username
elements.toolTip: A break-glass account on each host. Users sign in with their Entra credentials, not this one. Azure rejects administrator, admin, user, guest and root.

constraints.validationMessage: Lowercase letters and digits, 3 to 20 characters, starting with a letter.

elements.name: adminPassword
elements.toolTip: 12 to 123 characters, using three of: uppercase, lowercase, digit, symbol.

constraints.validationMessage: Between 12 and 123 characters.

elements.name: imageSku
elements.label: Image
elements.toolTip: Only 24H2 and newer are offered: cloud-only Entra Kerberos does not support older builds, so a 23H2 host deploys fine and then cannot mount a profile. The Microsoft 365 images live under a different marketplace offer, which the template works out from the SKU.

elements.name: osDiskType
elements.label: OS disk
elements.toolTip: Profiles live on the FSLogix share, not the OS disk, so premium disks buy less here than they would on a single-session desktop.

elements.name: osDiskSizeGB
elements.label: OS disk size
elements.toolTip: Disks grow but never shrink, so this can be raised later and not lowered. Profiles live on the FSLogix share, so it mostly matters for locally installed applications.

elements.name: acceleratedNetworking
elements.label: Accelerated networking
elements.toolTip: Untick this if you chose a B-series size. B-series does not support it and the deployment fails outright rather than carrying on without it.

elements.name: enrolWithIntune
elements.label: Enrol in Intune
elements.toolTip: Enrols each host during the Entra join. Requires Microsoft Entra ID P1.

elements.name: configureFslogix
elements.label: Configure FSLogix profile containers
elements.toolTip: The gallery image ships FSLogix installed but not configured. This points it at the profile share and enables cloud Kerberos, without which the host cannot authenticate to Azure Files. Ignored when storage is not deployed.

elements.name: fslogixProfileSizeMB
elements.label: Maximum profile size
elements.toolTip: A ceiling, not an allocation. The container grows as the profile does.

elements.name: restartAfterFslogix
elements.label: Restart hosts after configuring FSLogix
elements.toolTip: Cloud Kerberos is read by LSA at boot, so a host that is not restarted cannot authenticate to the share. Untick only if you will restart them yourself.

elements.name: timeZone
elements.label: Session host time zone
elements.toolTip: The host's own clock. For users spread across regions, use redirection below instead - or as well.

elements.name: enableTimeZoneRedirection
elements.label: Adopt the client's time zone in each session
elements.toolTip: Each session shows the time zone of the device connecting to it, rather than the host's. Takes effect for new sessions; no restart needed.

options.text: Session hosts are joined to Entra ID and registered with their host pool automatically. Whether the profile share is ready for them depends on the Entra ID tab.
